baselineChanges.note: Normalization impact compares this exact implementation with/without declaration-name correction. Baseline transitions also include concrete new implementation and newly reviewed test evidence; they are not feature percentages.

methodology: One row per pinned lexical declaration, retaining overload signature, source file, and line.
Implemented means the listed managed argument shape has a concrete adapter or audited direct implementation; it is not a claim of native binary or total pixel compatibility.
Partial means a callable/type exists with a documented difference, an untested semantic branch, or no completed signature-level audit. Method-name presence never upgrades a row to implemented.
Not-applicable is reserved for C# language constructs, process pointers, P/Invoke, or non-web UI integration. These are not counted as implemented features.
Missing means no matching browser type/member or an explicit unsupported overload.

Initializer expressions and generic method suffixes are normalized to field/method identities while originalName/originalKind and stable IDs remain preserved. Lexer corrections are counted independently from implementation changes.
This audit combines named overload adapters with evidence from native conformance, asset, font, document, surface, effect and GPU test suites. Untested semantic branches remain partial.
JavaScript mappings: ref/out structs use mutable objects; spans use arrays/typed arrays; numeric values use JavaScript Number; overload dispatch is dynamic.

Pinned-source corrections include System.Numerics row-vector SKMatrix44 storage, default Empty construction, midpoint-to-even checked Int32 rounding, exact value-zero SKRect.IsEmpty, degenerate rectangle intersection/union, and default warped text-on-path.
The inventory is lexical, includes preprocessor branches and obsolete forms, and does not expand inherited members. It is not compiler-produced metadata.
